source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. First, make sure you have an HTTPS server available and that you already know the URL of the image file.
2. Connect to the target server's BMC using SSH or otherwise.
3. After logging in to BMC, enter the OpenBMC console.
4. Image mount using OpenBMC's Web GUI. From the remote console interface, select Media -> Activate, then select Media -> Mount virtual media.
5. In the ""Mount Media File from Network"" option, enter the URL of your HTTP image file, for example: https://myserver.mycompany.com/media/myCD.ISO.
HTTPs — https://<URL>/<file path>/<image name>
6. From the ""Local Media Mounted"" section, select your software format (probably CD/DVD), then click ""Browse"" to find the software file, click ""Open"", then click ""Mount"".
7. Once it's done, you can go into the mounted ISO and do things like install an operating system.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: HTTP share/URL with a reachable HTTP image + BMC web + OS block tools
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Mount image via HTTPS: mount the install image via HTTP from the BMC web -> Media -> Mount Virtual Media (HTTP share/URL: ${VM_SHARE:?operator must set the virtual media share or server url}/${VM_PATH:?operator must set the path on the share}/${VM_IMAGE:?operator must set the image file name}), then confirm the image appears as a boot/block device sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsblk 2>&1; dmesg | tail -n 15 2>&1"; state-changing mount.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the OS block-device list + BMC web mount status so the user confirms the HTTP image mounted cleanly and is accessible.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: mounting an image shares it to the host and can autostart the OS; use a user-designated image URL and unmount after.

original_test_intent: Validate HTTPS-hosted BMC virtual-media access, Remote Console connectivity and host CD-ROM exposure; the source ambiguously also expects an Auto-install program without defining boot or installation completion.
original_method: An operator uses OpenBMC WebUI to mount an HTTPS image through Remote Console and may enter the mounted image's installer; OS device tools are only corroborative.
manual_activity: Engineering must select mount-only, boot-to-installer or installation scope. After correction, an operator controls WebUI/Remote Console; any boot or storage-changing installation needs separate destructive authorization.
required_inputs: exact HTTPS URL and immutable image hash
server certificate chain, trusted CA, authentication and redirect policy
isolated SUT with protected disks and boot baseline
BMC virtual-media SOP and expected virtual device
safety_requirements: Do not bypass TLS validation, embed credentials in URLs/logs or accept mutable/unverified media.
Do not boot, auto-install, partition or write storage without explicit target-disk and destructive-scope approval.
Reject `sshpass` and disabled host verification; preserve trusted before/after device and console evidence.
Prevent unapproved boot-target changes and prefer read-only media exposure where supported.
Deactivate media and verify exact device removal; stop on certificate, image, installer, boot or cleanup anomalies without retry.
agent_execution_scope: No execution until scope and HTTPS trust are resolved.
For an approved mount-only plan, validate certificate/image metadata and collect read-only BMC/console/device evidence around the operator action.
Do not operate WebUI, boot/install, modify storage or issue the final verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve the intended end state and approve HTTPS trust, image identity, target protection and cleanup.
Operate the attended WebUI/console flow under the approved scope.
Review complete evidence and issue PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic HTTP-labelled variables, unsafe SSH and `lsblk` cannot prove HTTPS trust, exact image identity, Remote Console behavior or authorized installer scope.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: None until the source scope is resolved. Then use certificate-validated HTTPS, an immutable image, the vendor WebUI/SOP, full before/after device evidence and explicit deactivation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: HTTPS/HTTP wording, WebUI steps, Auto-install Criteria, stray quote and 15/5-minute values remain preserved source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define independent checkpoints for TLS trust, image identity, Remote Console, virtual-media mount, exact host CD-ROM exposure and cleanup; authorize boot/install separately with a named target disk.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC/WebUI with documented HTTPS virtual-media support.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC, WebUI/browser, TLS/CA, image and host OS/tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor virtual-media and PKI documentation plus Project install/recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trust and integrity controls and separates mount from install only in the recommendation; Master remains unchanged.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Mount-only cannot claim boot/install, and installer appearance alone cannot prove successful installation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Scope, trust/image contract, disk protection and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A trusted but wrong bootable image can still alter boot flow or overwrite storage.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve mount/visibility only and must record that the ambiguous Auto-install coverage remains unverified. Any boot/install plan must identify the disk, Expected Result and recovery. HTTPS must retain certificate and image-integrity evidence.
expected_evidence: approved end state and isolated SUT/storage/boot baseline
exact URL, certificate chain/CA/auth policy and immutable image hash
BMC WebUI/Remote Console connection and mount artifacts
trusted pre/post device inventory identifying the exact virtual CD-ROM
deactivation, restored health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source says HTTPS but repeatedly labels the path HTTP, has incomplete numbered Criteria and conflates Remote Console/media exposure with an undefined Auto-install outcome.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mount-only and installation have incompatible core operations and safety acceptance, while the source also lacks an authoritative HTTPS trust/image contract. This requires an engineering scope decision, not merely a URL input.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes PARTIAL to BLOCKED because generic device collection does not resolve destructive end state or HTTPS trust.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and retains its TLS, integrity, disk and cleanup boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms the blocker while correcting its historical Round 02 characterization.

review_improvement: Separates transport trust, immutable media identity, reversible exposure and destructive installation so no one can claim one from evidence of another.
independent_technical_reasoning: HTTPS virtual-media mounting can be safely attended once trust and image identity are defined, but the source also expects an Auto-install program without saying whether it may boot or write storage. That changes the core operation and cannot be inferred. The record is therefore BLOCKED pending engineering scope/security decisions, not because ordinary inputs are missing and not as a DUT verdict.
